neighbours.label: the word that opens the time span of a rate, after a count of events ('... each year', 'in a typical year', 'in the next decade')
fire: Malaria still claims more than 400,000 lives each year.
The port handles roughly nine million containers in a typical year.
Some 60,000 hectares of forest are lost every year to logging.
A single oak can drop up to 10,000 acorns in any given season.
Around 1.3 million people die on the world's roads each year.
The charity expects to train 2,000 nurses in the next decade.
Nearly 50 billion chickens are slaughtered for food every year.
The glacier sheds about 30 metres of ice each summer.
quiet: Malaria still claims many lives across the tropics.
The port is the largest container terminal on the coast.
Large areas of forest have been lost to logging.
A single oak can live for several hundred years.
My grandfather died in the year the war ended.
The charity was founded a decade ago by two nurses.
Last year we raised chickens for the first time.
The glacier is visible from the village in summer.

notes: Card: peaks on ' in', ' each', ' every' before year/decade after counts of births and deaths; the + pole promotes ' every', ' per', ' each'. Probes: 'each year' 0.54, 'each season' 0.75, 'in a typical year' 0.54, 'in any given year' 0.50, 'every year' 0.22; 'per week' 0.01, 'last year' 0.19. A bare count with no period leaked 0.17-0.33, so some near misses may fire weakly.
